difficultyRationale: Tests the consumer side of lower-bounded wildcards and the safe type available when reading from them.
prompt: Given `List<? super Integer> values`, which operations are type-safe and compile? Select all that apply.
explanation: The captured element type is some unknown supertype of Integer, so adding an Integer is safe. Reading yields only Object without a cast because the actual supertype could be Integer, Number, or Object.

options.explanation: Integer can be stored in any List whose element type is Integer or a supertype of Integer.
Object is the universally safe static type for a value read from the lower-bounded wildcard.
The actual list could be a List<Object>, so the compiler cannot promise the retrieved value is an Integer.
The actual list could be List<Integer>, which cannot accept Double.

references.title: JLS 4.5.1 Type Arguments of Parameterized Types
